# War Scroll Column 12 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in War Scroll Column 12 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 12:1 — "Blessed be" vs. "Praise" — opening benediction formula

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Blessed be the-God of-Israel" | Literal rendering of barukh |
| LOGOS | "Blessed be the God of Israel" | Standard liturgical formula |
| PNEUMA | "Praise the God of Israel" | Dynamic rendering of barukh as an action |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "Blessed be" (EMET/LOGOS). barukh is a declarative blessing formula, not an imperative to praise.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 12:1 — "covenant-faithfulness" vs. "faithful love" — hesed rendering

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "covenant-faithfulness" | Project convention for hesed |
| LOGOS | "covenant-faithfulness" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "faithful love" | Warmer, more accessible English rendering |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "covenant-faithfulness" (EMET/LOGOS). Project convention established from Genesis 24 onward; consistency required.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 12:1-2 — "those who stumble" vs. "the weak and stumbling" — characterization

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "those-who-stumble" | Literal participle |
| LOGOS | "those who stumble" | Same, unhyphenated |
| PNEUMA | "the weak and stumbling" | Added "weak" for emphasis |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "those who stumble" (LOGOS). PNEUMA's addition of "weak" is interpretive.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 12:3 — "dumb" vs. "mute" vs. "speechless" — disability language

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-dumb" | Traditional biblical rendering of 'illem |
| LOGOS | "the mute" | Modern standard medical/biblical term |
| PNEUMA | "the speechless" | Avoids any potentially offensive term |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the mute" (LOGOS). Current standard English for 'illem; "dumb" is archaic and potentially misleading; "speechless" implies temporary condition.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 12:3 — "weak hands" vs. "feeble hands" vs. "untrained hands" — martial imagery

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "weak-hands" | Literal rendering of rapheh yadayim |
| LOGOS | "feeble hands" | Formal variant |
| PNEUMA | "untrained hands" | Interprets weakness as lack of training |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "feeble hands" (LOGOS). "Untrained" (PNEUMA) changes the meaning from weakness to inexperience; "feeble" captures the physical frailty intended.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 12:4 — "poor in spirit" vs. "humble in spirit" — sectarian self-designation

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "poor in-spirit" | Literal rendering of 'anawey ruach |
| LOGOS | "poor in spirit" | Standard rendering, parallels Matthew 5:3 |
| PNEUMA | "humble in spirit" | Interprets 'anaw as "humble" rather than "poor" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "poor in spirit" (EMET/LOGOS). This is a recognized sectarian self-designation; altering it to "humble" loses the socioeconomic dimension of 'anaw.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 12:5 — "perfect of way" vs. "perfect in the way" vs. "walk blamelessly"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "perfect-of-way" | Literal construct chain |
| LOGOS | "those who are perfect in the way" | Expanded for English grammar |
| PNEUMA | "those who walk blamelessly" | Dynamic rendering of tamimey derekh |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "those who are perfect in the way" (LOGOS). Preserves the sectarian self-designation; PNEUMA's rendering loses the noun-based identity marker.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 12:6-7 — "pit" vs. "abyss" — Belial's destiny

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-pit" | Literal rendering of shachat |
| LOGOS | "the pit" | Standard rendering |
| PNEUMA | "the abyss" | Heightened apocalyptic register |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the pit" (EMET/LOGOS). shachat means "pit/corruption"; "abyss" imports Greek apocalyptic vocabulary (abyssos) not present in the Hebrew.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 12:8 — "statutes of darkness" vs. "rules of darkness" — legal terminology

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "statutes of-darkness" | Literal rendering of chuqqey choshekh |
| LOGOS | "statutes of darkness" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "rules of darkness" | Simplified English |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "statutes of darkness" (EMET/LOGOS). chuqqim is a technical legal term best rendered "statutes" in biblical translation.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 12:10 — "poor ones" vs. "lowly" — divine assistance recipients

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-poor-ones" | Literal rendering of 'aniyyim |
| LOGOS | "the lowly" | Formal rendering capturing social status |
| PNEUMA | "the lowly" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "the lowly" (LOGOS/PNEUMA). Better English for the context; "poor ones" is redundant with "poor in spirit" above.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/PNEUMA.

---

## 12:11 — "prince" vs. "ruler" — angelic hierarchy

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "prince" | Literal rendering of sar |
| LOGOS | "prince" | Standard DSS rendering |
| PNEUMA | "ruler" | Modern equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "prince" (EMET/LOGOS). sar in angelic contexts is standard as "prince" (cf. Daniel 10:13, Michael as "prince").

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 12:13 — "strengthen light" vs. "exalt light" vs. "lift up the light"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "to-strengthen light" | Literal rendering |
| LOGOS | "to exalt light" | Formal elevation language |
| PNEUMA | "to lift up the light" | Dynamic equivalent |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "to strengthen light" (EMET). The Hebrew verb implies empowerment, not elevation; the parallel with "bring down darkness" favors a power-based verb.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET.

---

## 12:15 — "our fathers" vs. "our ancestors" — patriarchal language

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "our-fathers" | Literal rendering of 'avotenu |
| LOGOS | "our fathers" | Standard biblical rendering |
| PNEUMA | "our ancestors" | Gender-inclusive modern English |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "our fathers" (EMET/LOGOS). 'avot specifically means "fathers" in the patriarchal context; "ancestors" is acceptable English but loses the gendered specificity.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 12:16 — "seed" vs. "descendants" vs. "children" — generational language

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "their-seed" | Literal rendering of zar'am |
| LOGOS | "their descendants" | Standard formal English |
| PNEUMA | "their children" | Simplified, immediate |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted "their descendants" (LOGOS). "Seed" (EMET) is archaic; "children" (PNEUMA) implies only one generation; "descendants" captures the multigenerational scope.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

**Total disagreements:** 14
